correctness.rationale: The core classification exhausts all coalitions/proposals via Hare quota, with a separate guardian case. Fractional core+ is proved using both directions of the established payment characterization, an explicit strict-slack certificate and Cauchy--Schwarz lower bound on losing-common supporter reserves; ordinary-core and core+ counts are disjoint binomial cases. All committees are Pareto efficient by aggregate-utility invariants. The asymptotic is exact leading-term polynomial algebra; the packaged finite script tested 296 committees and independent LP certificates.

claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: Core+ implies ordinary core (Becker et al.); its converse fails (Berker et al.), and the guardian one-private case is known. Our proof classifies every size-k committee after replicating private alternatives, shows Pareto efficiency for every outcome, and computes exact counts. Neither implication nor the one-case example mathematically entails these counts without the new exhaustive structural analysis.

originality.rationale: No inspected primary publication or accessible prior finding implies the parameterized full ordinary-core/core+ census and fixed-seat vanishing core+ share with universal Pareto efficiency. Qualitative strictness, payment characterization and the r=1 one-private construction are explicitly prior and not claimed new.
residual_risks: A prior paper or note may already make the same clone-family counting argument without indexing it under core+ or frugal Lindahl priceability.
The two priceability papers use overlapping but not identical models; the argument here depends specifically on the core+ payment theorem, not on an unproved equivalence for other variants.
The asymptotic is instance-specific and fixed k, not a probabilistic election-model prevalence statement.

value.rationale: The classification answers a motivated quantitative axiom-comparison question: a known existence-strengthening can discard asymptotically almost all integral-core committees, not because those outcomes are Pareto dominated (indeed every committee in these elections is Pareto efficient), but because fractional objections distinguish them. Exact two-polynomial counts quantify selectivity for every fixed seat count k≥3 and all clone multiplicities r≥1; this is not a routine one-off counterexample or random unmotivated invariant.
